page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-56 is a memory-expanded compute-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 56 dedicated virtual CPUs across 28 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 448 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA. It contains no bundled local storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight significant multi-core compute capability and high memory throughput. The system achieves strong scores in stress-ng multi-core testing (82,175.9) and PassMark CPU metrics (63,298.87), accompanied by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,087.56. Parallel processing tasks perform efficiently, reflected in a Geekbench Clang software compilation score of 40,870.0 and ray tracing at 60,081.0. Multi-threaded decompression and PassMark database operations also register in the top quartile. However, single-core metrics are moderate, with Geekbench single-core recording 1,658.0 and uncached large-block write throughput measuring 67.79 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 allows resource-heavy in-memory processing without requiring excessive CPU overprovisioning. Key architectural tradeoffs include the omission of AVX-512 extensions and the reliance on external network volumes due to the absence of bundled local storage. This hardware profile fits memory-intensive multi-threaded workloads, including large in-memory databases, continuous integration build farms, data transformation pipelines, and medium-scale CPU-bound machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-56 is a memory-expanded instance featuring 56 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor across 28 physical cores and 448 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture with an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, the system integrates hardware cryptographic extensions and standard AVX support without AVX-512 or bundled local storage. In benchmark assessments, it demonstrates strong multi-threaded execution, registering 82,175.9 in stress-ng multi-core and 17,176.0 in Geekbench multi-core, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,087.56. While single-thread benchmarks and large-block memory writes show moderate throughput, the hardware delivers substantial compute density and memory capacity. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from pairing extensive memory directly with high core counts, minimizing idle CPU overhead for RAM-heavy applications. This configuration accommodates distributed compilation, in-memory databases, ETL pipelines, and CPU-based model inference.
